One instance per process \u2014 DuckDB takes a file lock,\n/// so extra isolates attach through [transferable] rather than reopening.\n///\n/// This library is deliberately Flutter-free so the DB tests run on the plain\n/// Dart VM. The app supplies the file path (see `lib/main.dart`).\nclass FleetDb {\n  FleetDb._(this._db, this.read);\n\n  final Database _db;\n\n  /// Read-only-by-convention connection for the UI isolate. DuckDB is MVCC,\n  /// so this sees a consistent snapshot while the writer commits.\n  final Connection read;\n\n  /// Pass to [inIsolate] to get a connection on another isolate.\n  TransferableDatabase get transferable => _db.transferable;\n\n  /// Opens [path] (`:memory:` for a throwaway db) and migrates it forward.\n  static Future<FleetDb> open(String path) async {\n    final db = await duckdb.open(path);\n    final conn = await duckdb.connect(db);\n    await _migrate(conn);\n    return FleetDb._(db, conn);\n  }\n\n  /// Runs [job] on its own isolate with its own connection.\n  ///\n  /// [job] must be a top-level or static function: it is sent across an\n  /// isolate boundary, so anything it closes over has to be sendable too.\n  static Future<R> inIsolate<R>(\n    TransferableDatabase transferable,\n    Future<R> Function(Connection) job,\n  ) {\n    return Isolate.run(() async {\n      final conn = await duckdb.connectWithTransferred(transferable);\n      try {\n        return await job(conn);\n      } finally {\n        await conn.dispose();\n      }\n    });\n  }\n\n  Future<void> close() async {\n    await read.dispose();\n    await _db.dispose();\n  }\n}\n\n/// Forward-only migrations, applied in one transaction each so a crash\n/// mid-upgrade leaves the previous version intact rather than a half-schema.\nFuture<void> _migrate(Connection conn) async {\n  await conn.execute(\n    'CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_version (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)',\n  );\n  final result = await conn.query(\n    'SELECT coalesce(max(version), 0) FROM schema_version',\n  );\n  final applied = (result.fetchOne()!.first as num).toInt();\n\n  for (var version = applied + 1; version <= migrations.length; version++) {\n    await conn.execute('BEGIN TRANSACTION');\n    try {\n      await conn.execute(migrations[version - 1]);\n      await conn.execute('INSERT INTO schema_version VALUES ($version)');\n      await conn.execute('COMMIT');\n    } catch (_) {\n      await conn.execute('ROLLBACK');\n      rethrow;\n    }\n  }\n}\nDART\ndart format lib/db/fleet_db.dart >/dev/null && dart analyze lib/db 2>&1 | tail -5",

as num).toInt(), (row[1] as num).toInt());\n}\n\n/// Runs a mutating statement and returns the row count DuckDB reports.\nFuture<int> _countOf(Connection conn, String sql) async {\n  final result = Accuracy is\n    // usually good and occasionally terrible \u2014 the bad fixes are what the\n    // geofence accuracy gate exists to throw away.\n    final reportsFix = vehicle.ignition || _tickCount % 6 == 0;\n    final fix = reportsFix\n        ? GeoFix(\n            lat: vehicle.lat,\n            lon: vehicle.lon,\n            accuracyM: _random.nextDouble() < 0.08\n                ? 60 + _random.nextDouble() * 180\n                : 4 + _random.nextDouble() * 12,\n          )\n        : null;\n\n    return TelemetryPacket(\n      vehicleId: vehicle.id,\n      eventTs: now,\n      signals: signals,\n      location: fix,\n    );\n  }\n\n  // --------------------------------------------------------------- fleet --\n\n  /// Builds one truck. Deterministic from its index, so the same seed always\n  /// produces the same fleet with the same problem children.\n  _SimulatedVehicle _buildVehicle(int index) {\n    const models = ['eT 1000', 'eT 1500', 'eHaul 400'];\n    const letters = 'ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ';\n    final regNo = 'KA01'\n        '${letters[index % letters.length]}${letters[(index ~/ 24) % letters.length]}'\n        '${(1000 + index * 7 % 9000)}';\n\n    return _SimulatedVehicle(\n      id: 'v${index.toString().padLeft(3, '0')}',\n      regNo: regNo,\n      model: models[index % models.length],\n      // Every seventh truck starts near the low-battery threshold and every\n      // eleventh runs hot, so the alert rules have something to fire on\n      // without waiting for a lucky random walk.\n      soc: index % 7 == 0 ? ```
## 1. Layout

```
lib/
  db/          schema.sql · migrations · DuckDbService (isolate, connections)
  ingest/      PacketSource (simulator) · IngestPipeline · Backfill
  derive/      SQL derivation: latest · alerts · transitions · trips
  query/       read-side queries returning plain Dart records
  features/    fleet · vehicle · alerts · geofences · trips  (Riverpod + widgets)
tool/
  bench.dart           cold start / p50 / p95 / memory harness
  export_ai_logs.sh    Claude session jsonl -> ai-logs/*.md
ai-logs/       uncurated AI conversation logs (deliverable 3)
```

No repository interfaces, no DAO layer, no abstract `TelemetryService`. One implementation each; a swap is a constructor argument, not an abstraction. Query functions return records/freezed models straight from SQL.

### Isolates

DuckDB is a single-writer, MVCC embedded engine. One process, so multiple connections against one instance are fine — readers get a snapshot while the writer commits.

- **Writer isolate** — owns ingest, derivation, backfill. Everything that mutates runs here, serialised, in transactions.
- **UI isolate** — read-only connection, queries on demand and on a *debounced* change ping (250 ms). A 3-hour backlog dump must not repaint the fleet list 500 times.

`dart_duckdb` exposes a transferable database handle for exactly this. Ingest batches are bounded (≤ 5k rows / 200 ms per transaction) so a backlog dump never holds a write lock long enough to stall reads.

---
```

### Claude — 2026-09-12T09:24:33.242Z
Ingest pipeline is built and running end to end.

```
lib/core/                     Failure · exceptions · UseCase/StreamUseCase · Result<T> · Clock
lib/features/telemetry_ingest/
  domain/        TelemetryPacket · IngestReceipt · IngestSnapshot · FleetVehicle
                 TelemetryRepository (interface)
                 SeedFleet · ObserveTelemetry · IngestPacketBatch · GetIngestSnapshot
  data/          TelemetryPacketModel · TelemetryPacketSource (interface)
                 SimulatedPacketSource + SimulatorConfig
                 TelemetryWriter (long-lived writer isolate)
                 TelemetryLocalDataSource + DuckDb impl · TelemetryRepositoryImpl
  presentation/  IngestController (GetxController) · IngestBinding · IngestPage
```

`domain` imports nothing outward. Concrete classes are named in exactly one place — `IngestBinding`. Every function has a doc comment explaining why, not what.

**Simulator** — seeded, so a run replays exactly. Injects all four failure modes the brief names: retransmits (identical event time, delivered a tick or two later, so dedupe is tested *across* batches not just within one), out-of-order delivery (held back, original event time kept), drops, and basement backlogs (buffered while dark, dumped in one burst). Signals report on different cadences, so packets carry a subset — which is why freshness is per-signal.

**Writer** — spawned once and kept; `Isolate.run` per batch costs more than the write. Batches bulk-append into two TEMP staging tables via DuckDB's row-wise appender (no statement per row, no escaping vehicle ids into SQL), then everything is set-based: `DISTINCT ON` for intra-batch duplicates, `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` for duplicates already on disk, the conditional upsert for late packets. Two transactions, watermark last, exactly as §3.4 specifies.

**Verified:** 33 tests pass, `flutter analyze` clean, macOS and Android both build. The real macOS app ran for 18s and left 40 vehicles / 4269 signal rows / 627 fixes / 240 latest-value rows / 40 watermarks on disk — read back by querying the app's actual database file, not from the UI.

The test that carries the design: `ingest_pipeline_test.dart` replays the same feed reversed, in ragged batches, with every third packet redelivered — log, latest, fixes and watermarks come back byte-identical to the in-order run.

Two things to flag. `conn.append(table, 'temp.main')` segfaults dart_duckdb (`unique_ptr is NULL`); the schema argument must be `null` for TEMP tables — found by probe, not by guessing. And the ingest monitor auto-starts the feed, since a screen whose job is showing the pipeline work shouldn't need a click.

**AI logs** exported to `ai-logs/` — 2 sessions, 419 turns, tool calls and results included. The exporter needed `--src`/`--match` flags: Claude Code groups transcripts by launch directory, and these sessions were started from a parent folder, so they sat beside unrelated work. `--match byte_beam_project` keeps only this project's conversations; I checked the output for cross-project content and found none.

ARCHITECTURE.md §1 is rewritten — it previously specified Riverpod and argued *against* repository interfaces. Your instruction overrides that, so the doc now documents what the code does; worth knowing the doc changed position, since you'll defend it live. Everything uncommitted.

### Claude — 2026-09-12T20:04:22.413Z
Fleet home is built. Feature A is done.

```
lib/features/fleet/
  domain/        VehicleStatus · AlertSeverity · FleetFilter
                 FleetVehicleSummary · FleetOverview
                 FleetRepository · GetFleetOverview
  data/          FleetLocalDataSource (the SQL) + DuckDb impl
                 FleetVehicleSummaryModel · FleetRepositoryImpl
  presentation/  FleetController · FleetBinding · FleetPage
                 StatusChip/AlertBadge · FleetFilterBar · VehicleTile · FleetEmptyState
lib/core/db/database_pulse.dart
```

Fleet is now home; the ingest monitor moved behind an app-bar action.

**Status and counts are both SQL.** One `scored` CTE — pivot `vehicle_signal_latest` with `FILTER`, union in `location_fix` for the vehicle-level last ping, cross-join thresholds from `signal_spec` — then two queries over it: `GROUP BY status` for the chips, `WHERE status = …` for the rows. Counts span the whole fleet, never just what's on screen; there's a test for that, because counting the returned rows is the easy bug.

**A test forced a design correction.** I had the status ladder checking each signal against its own `signal_spec.max_age_sec` (5 min). But OFFLINE is a 10-minute window, so that leaves a dead band: a truck reporting every six minutes is online yet every signal is stale, and it reads STOPPED while visibly driving. The ladder now scores freshness against the same 10-minute window — status is a vehicle-level claim, so it gets the vehicle's liveness window. The alert badge keeps the per-signal window, since the brief scopes thresholds to fresh readings and a threshold is a claim about one signal. That's logged as ambiguity 14 in ARCHITECTURE.md, and ambiguity 1 now names which window it meant.

**Refresh** goes through `DatabasePulse` — the writer bumps a counter after commit, the fleet controller debounces it at 250 ms. A backlog dump commits several batches back to back and repaints once; there's a test that eight pings produce one reload.

**Verified:** 73 tests pass (20 SQL status/badge/chip cases, 5 controller, 7 widget, 8 end-to-end), `flutter analyze` clean, macOS and Android both build. import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:get/get.dart';
import 'package:path/path.dart' as p;
import 'package:path_provider/path_provider.dart';

import 'core/db/database_pulse.dart';
import 'db/fleet_db.dart';
import 'features/fleet/presentation/bindings/fleet_binding.dart';
import 'features/fleet/presentation/pages/fleet_page.dart';
import 'features/telemetry_ingest/presentation/bindings/ingest_binding.dart';
import 'features/vehicle_detail/presentation/bindings/vehicle_detail_binding.dart';

/// Opens the database and builds the object graph before the first frame.
///
/// Deliberately not lazy. Opening DuckDB and spawning the writer isolate are
/// both async, and a screen that builds before its writer exists would have to
/// carry a "not ready yet" state that never means anything useful.
Future<void> main() async {
  WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();

  final db = await FleetDb.open(await databasePath());
  Get.put<FleetDb>(db, permanent: true);
  Get.put(DatabasePulse(), permanent: true);

  await IngestBinding(db: db).dependenciesAsync();
  FleetBinding(db: db).dependencies();
  VehicleDetailBinding(db: db).dependencies();

  runApp(const FleetConsoleApp());
}

/// Where the database lives. Application support, not documents or cache:
/// it is app-private state the OS must not evict.
Future<String> databasePath() async {
  final dir = await getApplicationSupportDirectory();
  await dir.create(recursive: true);
  return p.join(dir.path, 'fleet.duckdb');
}

/// Root widget. `GetMaterialApp` rather than `MaterialApp` so routes and

The cursor mechanism is\n  real because the simulator is a positioned, replayable source.\n* The watermark advances with no derivation behind it yet. Derived tables are\n  class D \u2014 dropped and rebuilt \u2014 so the first derivation pass rebuilds from\n  the log regardless.\n* `DatabasePulse` is a counter, not a change feed. to_seconds(s.max_age_sec) THEN 'STALE'\n         WHEN (s.crit_lo IS NOT NULL AND l.value < s.crit_lo)\n           OR (s.crit_hi IS NOT NULL AND l.value > s.crit_hi)\n           OR (s.warn_lo IS NOT NULL AND l.value < s.warn_lo)\n           OR (s.warn_hi IS NOT NULL AND l.value > s.warn_hi) THEN 'ALERT'\n         ELSE 'NORMAL'\n       END AS verdict\nFROM signal_spec s\nLEFT JOIN vehicle_signal_latest l\n  ON l.signal = s.signal AND l.vehicle_id = $2\nORDER BY list_position(\n  ['soc', 'range_km', 'speed', 'battery_temp', 'odometer', 'ignition'], s.signal)\n```\n\nOrder matters and it is deliberate: **staleness is checked before the\nthresholds.** A reading of 4 % SOC that arrived forty minutes ago is STALE, not\nALERT. ```

**Readings register** is driven by a LEFT JOIN *from* `signal_spec`, not a hard-coded list — adding a signal to config adds a row, and a signal that has never reported still gets one, which is exactly the "—, no pill" case. Order in the `CASE` is the substance: **staleness is checked before thresholds.** 4% SOC that arrived 40 minutes ago is STALE, not ALERT — asserting "alert" claims something about a value we no longer trust, and "normal" claims the opposite. That's why STALE is a third verdict rather than a flag, and why its pill is grey. Last ping gets an age but no pill; the status chip beside it already makes the liveness claim.

**History** is the one query that touches the event log, bucketed in SQL. Two corrections, both caught by running it rather than reasoning: bucket width has to come from the span the data actually covers (a freshly started app has 20 seconds of history inside a 24-hour window and collapsed to one point), and buckets align to the first reading rather than absolute epoch, or the partial bucket at each end puts the count one over the cap. Sparkline is ~40 lines of `CustomPainter` on a fixed 0–100% axis — auto-scaling makes a battery drifting 61→63% look like a cliff.

**The status ladder moved to `lib/db/`.** The detail header and the fleet list make the same claim about the same vehicle; two copies of that `CASE` would drift.

**Two things worth knowing.** DuckDB 1.2.1 cannot resolve a *second* named parameter in a statement opening with `WITH` — it reports two parameters, then fails the name lookup. Everything is now positional `$1`/`$2`, with the contract documented on the shared CTE. And I moved ingest startup out of `onInit` into the binding: `onInit` can't be awaited, so `main()` reached `runApp` while the roster seed was still in flight. That's a real race regardless; I first blamed it for a run that ingested nothing, but I couldn't reproduce that run afterward, so treat the lifecycle story as unconfirmed — the explicit `await controller.bootstrap()` is the right shape either way. It's now pinned by `ingest_binding_test.dart`, which exists because every other test passed while a running app wrote nothing.

**Verified:** 108 tests, analyzer clean, macOS builds and runs. Queried the register straight from the database the real app left behind — SOC 14.7% → ALERT, everything else NORMAL, 35 log readings into 26 points.

**Docs** — `docs/01`–`03`, same shape each: what it does, files, data flow, the SQL, decisions with rejected alternatives, a table mapping every claim to the test that pins it, and known limits. The index lists the three unbuilt features so the gap is explicit.

skipped: history is SOC-only and the window is a fixed 24h — both are parameters, not redesigns. AI logs refreshed; everything uncommitted.

## 6. Alerts

Evaluated over `vehicle_signal_latest ⋈ signal_spec`, **fresh readings only**, after every ingest batch.

| Alert | Condition | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| `battery_low` | SOC < 20 % | warning |
| `battery_low` | SOC < 10 % | **critical** (same row, escalated) |
| `battery_overheat` | battery_temp > 45 °C | critical |

The two SOC alerts are one row whose `severity` moves warning ⇄ critical. Recovering from 8 % to 15 % de-escalates in place; it does not resolve and re-raise.

**Dismissal.** Sheet order is fixed: *I am on it* · *Wrong alert* · *Something else…*. The dismissal is written to DuckDB immediately and UNDO clears `dismissed_at`. It is not held in memory for 5 seconds — local-first means the database is the truth, and if the app dies mid-window the dismissal stands. That is the honest trade; the alternative loses a user's explicit action to a crash.

**Resolution is independent.** The evaluator clears an alert when its condition clears, dismissed or not. A dismissed alert whose condition never clears simply stays hidden until the condition clears and re-triggers — dismissal suppresses the *episode*, not the *rule*.

---

/// The status ladder, in one place.
///
/// Lives beside the schema rather than inside a feature because it is a
/// property of the data, not of a screen: the fleet list and the vehicle
/// detail header both make the same claim about the same vehicle, and two
/// copies of this `CASE` would eventually disagree.
library;

/// How long without any report before a vehicle counts as offline.
const offlineAfter = 'INTERVAL 10 MINUTE';

/// The shared prefix: every fleet query selects from `scored`.
///
/// **Parameter contract: `$1` is the instant to evaluate freshness against**,
/// and a statement built on this CTE binds it first. Numbered parameters
/// rather than named ones because DuckDB 1.2.1 cannot resolve a *second*
/// named parameter in a statement that opens with `WITH` — it reports two
/// parameters and then fails the name lookup for the one outside the CTE.
/// Numbered binding has no such problem, and a repeated `$1` still counts
/// once.
///
/// Four stages, each earning its place:
///
/// * `latest`  — pivots the long-format latest table into one row per vehicle.
///   `FILTER` keeps it to a single pass, and the per-signal timestamps come
///   along because freshness is judged per signal, not per vehicle.
/// * `ping`    — vehicle-level last ping is the newest event time from *any*
///   signal or position report (§10, ambiguity 2).
/// * `spec`    — alert thresholds and staleness windows read from
///   `signal_spec`, so they are configuration rather than constants buried in
///   this string.
/// * `scored`  — the first-match-wins status and the alert badge.
///
/// Two windows, deliberately different, because they back claims of different
/// scope:
///
/// * The **status ladder** judges freshness against the same 10-minute window
///   that decides OFFLINE. Status is a vehicle-level claim, so its inputs get
///   the vehicle's own liveness window. A speed 40 minutes old cannot claim
///   MOVING, but a truck reporting every six minutes is still MOVING —
///   scoring the ladder against the 5-minute per-signal window instead would
///   leave a dead band between 5 and 10 minutes where every online vehicle
///   reads STOPPED (§10, ambiguity 1).
/// * The **alert badge** judges freshness per signal against
///   `signal_spec.max_age_sec`, because the brief scopes thresholds to fresh
///   readings and a threshold is a claim about one signal, not the vehicle.
///
/// STOPPED is the `ELSE`: both "ignition off" and the documented fallback when
/// the deciding signals are too stale to judge.
const scoredCte =
    '''

  SELECT vehicle_id,
         max(value)    FILTER (WHERE signal = 'soc')          AS soc,

import 'dart:isolate';

import 'package:dart_duckdb/dart_duckdb.dart';

import 'schema.dart';

/// The embedded database. One instance per process — DuckDB takes a file lock,
/// so extra isolates attach through [transferable] rather than reopening.
///
/// This library is deliberately Flutter-free so the DB tests run on the plain
/// Dart VM. The app supplies the file path (see `lib/main.dart`).
class FleetDb {
  FleetDb._(this._db, this.read);

  final Database _db;

  /// Read-only-by-convention connection for the UI isolate. DuckDB is MVCC,
  /// so this sees a consistent snapshot while the writer commits.
  final Connection read;

  /// Pass to [inIsolate] to get a connection on another isolate.
  TransferableDatabase get transferable => _db.transferable;

  /// Opens [path] (`:memory:` for a throwaway db) and migrates it forward.
  static Future<FleetDb> open(String path) async {
    final db = await duckdb.open(path);
    final conn = await duckdb.connect(db);
    await _migrate(conn);
    return FleetDb._(db, conn);
  }

  /// Runs [job] on its own isolate with its own connection.
  ///
  /// [job] must be a top-level or static function: it is sent across an
  /// isolate boundary, so anything it closes over has to be sendable too.
  static Future<R> inIsolate<R>(
    TransferableDatabase transferable,
    Future<R> Function(Connection) job,
  ) {
    return Isolate.run(() async {
      final conn = await duckdb.connectWithTransferred(transferable);
      try {
        return await job(conn);
      } finally {
        await conn.dispose();
      }
    });
  }

  Future<void> close() async {
    await read.dispose();
    await _db.dispose();
  }
}

/// Forward-only migrations, applied in one transaction each so a crash
/// mid-upgrade leaves the previous version intact rather than a half-schema.
Future<void> _migrate(Connection conn) async {
  await conn.execute(
    'CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_version (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY)',
  );
  final result = await conn.query(
    'SELECT coalesce(max(version), 0) FROM schema_version',
  );
  final applied = (result.fetchOne()!.first as num).toInt();

  for (var version = applied + 1; version <= migrations.length; version++) {
    await conn.execute('BEGIN TRANSACTION');
    try {
      await conn.execute(migrations[version - 1]);
      await conn.execute('INSERT INTO schema_version VALUES ($version)');
      await conn.execute('COMMIT');
    } catch (_) {
      await conn.execute('ROLLBACK');
      rethrow;
    }
  }
}

import 'vehicle_status.dart';

/// The chip row above the fleet list.
///
/// [all] is deliberately part of the same enum rather than a nullable status:
/// the UI needs a fifth chip with its own count, and modelling it as "no
/// filter" would mean a special case at every call site.
enum FleetFilter {
  all,
  moving,
  idle,
  stopped,
  offline;

  /// The status this filter selects, or null for [all].
  VehicleStatus? get status => switch (this) {
    FleetFilter.all => null,
    FleetFilter.moving => VehicleStatus.moving,
    FleetFilter.idle => VehicleStatus.idle,
    FleetFilter.stopped => VehicleStatus.stopped,
    FleetFilter.offline => VehicleStatus.offline,
  };

  /// Chip label.
  String get label => switch (this) {
    FleetFilter.all => 'All',
    FleetFilter.moving => 'Moving',
    FleetFilter.idle => 'Idle',
    FleetFilter.stopped => 'Stopped',
    FleetFilter.offline => 'Offline',
  };
}

import 'fleet_filter.dart';
import 'fleet_vehicle_summary.dart';

/// Everything the fleet screen renders in one value.
///
/// Rows and counts travel together because they are read in the same refresh
/// and must agree: a chip that says "12 moving" beside a list of 9 is worse
/// than either number being slightly stale.
class FleetOverview {
  const FleetOverview({
    required this.filter,
    required this.vehicles,
    required this.counts,
  });

  const FleetOverview.empty()
    : filter = FleetFilter.all,
      vehicles = const [],
      counts = const {};

  /// Which chip produced [vehicles].
  final FleetFilter filter;

  /// The rows matching [filter], already ordered.
  final List<FleetVehicleSummary> vehicles;

  /// Live count per chip, computed in SQL over the whole fleet — not by
  /// counting [vehicles], which only holds the current filter.
  final Map<FleetFilter, int> counts;

  /// Count for one chip, zero when no vehicle is in that state.
  int countFor(FleetFilter filter) => counts[filter] ?? 0;

  /// True when the fleet has vehicles but this filter matched none — the case
  /// that gets an empty state rather than a blank screen.
  bool get isFilteredEmpty => vehicles.isEmpty && countFor(FleetFilter.all) > 0;

  /// True when there is no fleet at all yet.
  bool get isFleetEmpty => countFor(FleetFilter.all) == 0;
}

import 'package:dart_duckdb/dart_duckdb.dart';

import '../../../../core/error/exceptions.dart';
import '../../../../db/vehicle_status_sql.dart';
import '../../domain/entities/fleet_filter.dart';
import '../../domain/entities/fleet_overview.dart';
import '../../domain/entities/vehicle_status.dart';
import '../models/fleet_vehicle_summary_model.dart';

/// Reads the fleet list out of DuckDB.
///
/// The whole read path is `vehicle` (500 rows) joined to
/// `vehicle_signal_latest` (500 x 6) and `signal_spec` (6). No scan of the
/// multi-million-row log happens here, which is the entire reason
/// `vehicle_signal_latest` is maintained on ingest.
abstract class FleetLocalDataSource {
  /// Rows for [filter] plus the count for every chip, read at instant [now].
  Future<FleetOverview> overview(FleetFilter filter, DateTime now);
}

/// DuckDB implementation.
class DuckDbFleetLocalDataSource implements FleetLocalDataSource {
  const DuckDbFleetLocalDataSource(this._read);

  /// The UI isolate's read connection. Sees an MVCC snapshot, so a commit in
  /// the writer never blocks the list.
  final Connection _read;

  @override
  Future<FleetOverview> overview(FleetFilter filter, DateTime now) async {
    try {
      // Two queries, both over the same CTE: the counts must span the whole
      // fleet while the rows are narrowed to one chip. Counting the returned
      // rows instead would make every chip read "the number you can see".
      final counts = await _counts(now);
      final vehicles = await _vehicles(filter, now);
      return FleetOverview(filter: filter, vehicles: vehicles, counts: counts);
    } catch (error) {
      throw LocalDatabaseException('fleet overview query failed', error);
    }
  }

  /// Count per status, plus the total for the "All" chip.
  Future<Map<FleetFilter, int>> _counts(DateTime now) async {
    final result = await _query(
      '$scoredCte SELECT status, count(*) FROM scored GROUP BY status',
      now,
    );

    final counts = {for (final filter in FleetFilter.values) filter: 0};
    var total = 0;
    for (final row in result.fetchAll()) {
      final status = VehicleStatus.fromSql(row[0]! as String);
      final count = (row[1]! as num).toInt();
      total += count;
      counts[_filterFor(status)] = count;
    }
    counts[FleetFilter.all] = total;
    return counts;
  }

  /// The rows for one chip, ordered by registration so the list is stable
  /// between refreshes — an order that jumps as speeds change is unreadable.
  Future<List<FleetVehicleSummaryModel>> _vehicles(
    FleetFilter filter,
    DateTime now,
  ) async {
    final status = filter.status;
    final where = status == null ? '' : "WHERE status = '${status.sqlName}'";
    final result = await _query(
      '$scoredCte SELECT vehicle_id, reg_no, model, status, soc, range_km, '
      'speed, last_ping, alert_severity FROM scored $where ORDER BY reg_no',
      now,
    );
    return [
      for (final row in result.fetchAll())
        FleetVehicleSummaryModel.fromRow(row),
    ];
  }

  /// Runs a statement built on [scoredCte], binding the instant to compare
  /// freshness against.
  ///
  /// `now` is bound rather than taken from SQL's own `now()` so tests can pin
  /// it — a fleet list whose rules depend on the wall clock is untestable.
  Future<ResultSet> _query(String sql, DateTime now) async {
    final statement = await _read.prepare(sql);
    try {
      statement.bindParams([now]);
      return await statement.execute();
    } finally {
      await statement.dispose();
    }
  }

  /// Maps a status back to the chip that selects it.
  FleetFilter _filterFor(VehicleStatus status) => switch (status) {
    VehicleStatus.moving => FleetFilter.moving,
    VehicleStatus.idle => FleetFilter.idle,
    VehicleStatus.stopped => FleetFilter.stopped,
    VehicleStatus.offline => FleetFilter.offline,
  };
}

import 'telemetry_writer_isolate.dart';

/// Everything the feature does to local storage.
///
/// Abstract so the repository can be tested against a fake, and so the
/// DuckDB-specific parts stay in one file.
abstract class TelemetryLocalDataSource {
  /// Installs the fleet roster. Returns rows inserted; zero if already seeded.
  Future<int> seedFleet(List<FleetVehicle> vehicles);

  /// Writes one batch durably.
  Future<IngestReceiptModel> applyBatch(List<TelemetryPacketModel> batch);

  /// Reads current totals off disk.
  Future<IngestSnapshot> snapshot();

  /// Stops the writer.
  Future<void> dispose();
}

/// DuckDB-backed implementation.
///
/// Writes go to the [TelemetryWriter] isolate; reads use the UI isolate's own
/// connection, which sees an MVCC snapshot and is never blocked by a commit
/// in flight.
class DuckDbTelemetryLocalDataSource implements TelemetryLocalDataSource {
  DuckDbTelemetryLocalDataSource._(this._db, this._writer);

  final FleetDb _db;
  final TelemetryWriter _writer;

  /// Read connection, exposed for the feature screens that query directly.
  Connection get read => _db.read;

  /// Spawns the writer against an already-open database.
  static Future<DuckDbTelemetryLocalDataSource> create(FleetDb db) async {
    final writer = await TelemetryWriter.spawn(db.transferable);
    return DuckDbTelemetryLocalDataSource._(db, writer);
  }

  @override
  Future<int> seedFleet(List<FleetVehicle> vehicles) {
    // Flattened to rows here rather than in the writer so the isolate boundary
    // carries plain data and not another domain type.
    final rows = [
      for (final vehicle in vehicles)
        <Object?>[vehicle.vehicleId, vehicle.regNo, vehicle.model],
    ];
    return _writer.seedFleet(rows);
  }

  @override
  Future<IngestReceiptModel> applyBatch(List<TelemetryPacketModel> batch) =>
      _writer.applyBatch(batch);

  /// One query for all four numbers — four round trips would cost more than
  /// the aggregation does.
  @override
  Future<IngestSnapshot> snapshot() async {
    try {
      final result = await _db.read.query('''
        SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM vehicle),
               (SELECT count(*) FROM signal_reading),
               (SELECT count(*) FROM location_fix),
               (SELECT max(processed_through) FROM ingest_watermark)
      ''');
      final row = result.fetchOne()!;
      return IngestSnapshot(
        vehicles: (row[0] as num).toInt(),
        signalRows: (row[1] as num).toInt(),
        locationRows: (row[2] as num).toInt(),
        newestEventTs: row[3] as DateTime?,
      );
    } catch (error) {
      throw LocalDatabaseException('snapshot query failed', error);
    }
  }

  @override
  Future<void> dispose() => _writer.dispose();
}

/// Drives the vehicle detail screen.
///
/// One permanent controller rather than one per vehicle keyed by tag: only one
/// detail screen is open at a time, so [open] switching the subject is simpler
/// than a tagged instance per vehicle and leaves nothing to dispose.
class VehicleDetailController extends GetxController {
  VehicleDetailController({
    required GetVehicleDetail getVehicleDetail,
    required DatabasePulse pulse,
    required Clock clock,
    this.refreshDebounce = const Duration(milliseconds: 250),
  }) : _getVehicleDetail = getVehicleDetail,
       _pulse = pulse,
       _clock = clock;

  final GetVehicleDetail _getVehicleDetail;
  final DatabasePulse _pulse;
  final Clock _clock;

  /// How long to settle after a write before re-querying.
  final Duration refreshDebounce;

  /// Vehicle currently on screen, or empty before the first [open].
  final vehicleId = ''.obs;

  /// Loaded detail, or null while loading or when the vehicle is unknown.
  final detail = Rxn<VehicleDetail>();

  /// True until the first query for the current vehicle returns.
  final isLoading = true.obs;

  /// True when the roster has no such vehicle.
  final notFound = false.obs;

  /// Last error, or empty.
  final error = ''.obs;

  /// The instant the visible ages and verdicts were measured against.
  ///
  /// Held so the UI renders ages from the same reading the verdicts used. A
  /// row whose pill says STALE while its age reads "2s ago" is worse than a
  /// clock that ticks only on refresh.
  final evaluatedAt = Rxn<DateTime>();

  @override
  void onInit() {
    super.onInit();
    debounce<int>(_pulse.revision, (_) => _reload(), time: refreshDebounce);
  }

  /// Switches the screen to [id] and loads it.
  Future<void> open(String id) async {
    if (vehicleId.value != id) {
      vehicleId.value = id;
      detail.value = null;
      isLoading.value = true;
      notFound.value = false;
      error.value = '';
    }
    await _reload();
  }

  /// Re-queries the current vehicle. Does nothing before the first [open].
  Future<void> _reload() async {
    final id = vehicleId.value;
    if (id.isEmpty) return;

    final now = _clock.nowUtc();
    final result = await _getVehicleDetail(
      VehicleDetailParams(vehicleId: id, now: now),
    );
    switch (result) {
      case Ok(:final VehicleDetail? value):
        detail.value = value;
        notFound.value = value == null;
        evaluatedAt.value = now;
        error.value = '';
      case Err(:final failure):
        error.value = failure.message;
    }
    isLoading.value = false;
  }

  /// Pull-to-refresh and the retry button.
  Future<void> refreshNow() => _reload();
}

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dart_duckdb/dart_duckdb.dart';
import 'package:dart_duckdb/open.dart';

/// dart_duckdb loads its native library out of the app bundle on device. Under
/// `flutter test` the host VM has loaded nothing, and the package's own test
/// fallback points at paths inside the dart_duckdb monorepo — so point it at
/// the host copy fetched by `tool/fetch_duckdb_lib.sh`.
///
/// Spawned isolates need no equivalent call: once this isolate has opened the
/// library its symbols are in the process, which is the first thing
/// dart_duckdb looks for.
void useHostDuckDb() {
  final (os, name) = Platform.isMacOS
      ? (OperatingSystem.macOS, 'libduckdb.dylib')
      : (OperatingSystem.linux, 'libduckdb.so');
  final lib = File('.duckdb/$name');
  if (!lib.existsSync()) {
    throw StateError('${lib.path} missing — run tool/fetch_duckdb_lib.sh');
  }
  open.overrideFor(os, lib.absolute.path);
}

Either one hides the row, and only resolution ends the episode.\nconst openAlertPredicate = 'resolved_at IS NULL AND dismissed_at IS NULL';\n\n/// Scratch table holding \"what is wrong right now\", rebuilt every evaluation.\n///\n/// A table rather than a CTE shared across the three lifecycle statements,\n/// because a CTE cannot span statements and repeating it three times would\n/// give three chances to drift. It is TEMP, so it belongs to the writer's\n/// connection and never touches the file \u2014 the same idiom as the ingest\n/// staging tables.\nconst alertConditionDdl = '''\nCREATE TEMP TABLE IF NOT EXISTS staging_alert_condition (\n  vehicle_id TEXT, alert_type TEXT, severity TEXT\n);\n''';\n\n/// Empties the scratch table before each evaluation.\nconst clearAlertCondition = 'DELETE FROM staging_alert_condition';\n\n/// Recomputes every currently-breached threshold from fresh readings.\n///\n/// Fleet-wide rather than limited to the vehicles in this batch. A vehicle\n/// that stops reporting never appears in a batch again, and its alert must\n/// still resolve when the reading it was raised on goes stale \u2014 so the set of\n/// vehicles to re-check is \"all of them\", not \"the ones that just spoke\".\n/// At 500 vehicles x 6 signals that is a few thousand rows per tick.\n///\n/// `fresh` nulls out any reading older than its own `signal_spec.max_age_sec`,\n/// which is what makes \"thresholds apply to fresh readings only\" a property of\n/// the data rather than a rule each query remembers to apply. The two SOC\n/// bands are one row with two severities, not two alerts.\nconst insertAlertCondition = r'''\nINSERT INTO staging_alert_condition\nWITH spec AS (\n  SELECT max(max_age_sec) FILTER (WHERE signal = 'soc')          AS soc_age,\n         max(max_age_sec) FILTER (WHERE signal = 'battery_temp') AS temp_age,\n         max(warn_lo)     FILTER (WHERE signal = 'soc')          AS soc_warn_lo,\n         max(crit_lo)     FILTER (WHERE signal = 'soc')          AS soc_crit_lo,\n         max(crit_hi)     FILTER (WHERE signal = 'battery_temp') AS temp_crit_hi\n  FROM signal_spec\n),\nfresh AS (\n  SELECT l.vehicle_id,\n         max(l.value) FILTER (\n           WHERE l.signal = 'soc'\n             AND l.event_ts >= $1 - to_seconds(s.soc_age)\n         ) AS soc,\n         max(l.value) FILTER (\n           WHERE l.signal = 'battery_temp'\n             AND l.event_ts >= $1 - to_seconds(s.temp_age)\n         ) AS battery_temp\n  FROM vehicle_signal_latest l CROSS JOIN spec s\n  GROUP BY l.vehicle_id\n)\nSELECT f.vehicle_id,\n       'battery_low',\n       CASE WHEN f.soc < s.soc_crit_lo THEN 'critical' ELSE 'warning' END\nFROM fresh f CROSS JOIN spec s\nWHERE f.soc < s.soc_warn_lo\nUNION ALL\nSELECT f.vehicle_id, 'battery_overheat', 'critical'\nFROM fresh f CROSS JOIN spec s\nWHERE f.battery_temp > s.temp_crit_hi\n''';\n\n/// Closes every open episode whose condition is no longer breached.\n///\n/// Ignores `dismissed_at` deliberately: an alert the user waved away still\n/// resolves when the truck is plugged in. Dismissal suppresses the episode,\n/// resolution ends it, and only an ended episode can be raised again.\nconst resolveClearedAlerts = r'''\nUPDATE alert SET resolved_at = $1\nWHERE resolved_at IS NULL\n  AND NOT EXISTS (\n    SELECT 1 FROM staging_alert_condition c\n    WHERE c.vehicle_id = alert.vehicle_id\n      AND c.alert_type = alert.alert_type\n  )\n''';\n\n/// Moves an open episode between severities in place.\n///\n/// This is the escalation rule from the brief: SOC 18% -> 8% is the *same*\n/// alert turning critical, not a second one. Recovering to 15% walks it back\n/// down the same way. `escalated_at` is stamped only on the way up and kept\n/// afterwards, so \"this one went critical at some point\" survives a recovery.\nconst rescoreOpenAlerts = r'''\nUPDATE alert SET\n  severity = c.severity,\n  escalated_at = CASE\n    WHEN c.severity = 'critical' AND alert.severity <> 'critical' THEN $1\n    ELSE alert.escalated_at\n  END\nFROM staging_alert_condition c\nWHERE c.vehicle_id = alert.vehicle_id\n  AND c.alert_type = alert.alert_type\n  AND alert.resolved_at IS NULL\n  AND alert.severity <> c.severity\n''';\n\n/// Opens an episode for every breach that does not already have one.\n///\n/// `NOT EXISTS` over open episodes is what keeps this idempotent: running the\n/// evaluator twice on the same state raises nothing the second time, which is\n/// the property that lets it run after every batch without bookkeeping.\n///\n/// The id is derived rather than random so a replay produces the same row.\n/// Two episodes of one type on one vehicle cannot share an instant \u2014 the first\n/// has to resolve before the second can be raised, and resolution and raising\n/// never happen in the same pass.\nconst raiseNewAlerts = r'''\nINSERT INTO alert\n  (alert_id, vehicle_id, alert_type, severity, raised_at, escalated_at)\nSELECT c.vehicle_id || '|' || c.alert_type || '|' || CAST(epoch_ms($1) AS TEXT),\n       c.vehicle_id,\n       c.alert_type,\n       c.severity,\n       $1,\n       CASE WHEN c.severity = 'critical' THEN $1 END\nFROM staging_alert_condition c\nWHERE NOT EXISTS (\n  SELECT 1 FROM alert a\n  WHERE a.vehicle_id = c.vehicle_id\n    AND a.alert_type = c.alert_type\n    AND a.resolved_at IS NULL\n)\n''';\n\n/// Hides one alert and records why. `$1` id, `$2` instant, `$3` reason.\nconst dismissAlert = r'''\nUPDATE alert SET dismissed_at = $2, dismiss_reason = $3 WHERE alert_id = $1\n''';\n\n/// Puts a dismissed alert back. A separate statement rather than [dismissAlert]\n/// with null parameters: binding a typed NULL through the prepared-statement\n/// API is one more thing that can be wrong at runtime, and `SET x = NULL` in\n/// the text cannot be.\nconst restoreAlert = r'''\nUPDATE alert SET dismissed_at = NULL, dismiss_reason = NULL WHERE alert_id = $1\n''';\n\n/// Which signal each alert type watches, as a two-row inline relation.\n///\n/// Code-level configuration, so a table would mean a migration to say the same\n/// thing. Joined into the read query to pick up the current value, its unit\n/// and its label from `signal_spec` rather than hard-coding \"%\" and \"C\".\nconst alertSignalMap =\n    \"(VALUES ('battery_low', 'soc'), ('battery_overheat', 'battery_temp'))\"\n    ' AS m(alert_type, signal)';\nDART\necho ok",

/// Human-readable ages, used wherever the UI says how old something is.
///
/// In `core` rather than beside one widget because the readings register, the
/// alert cards and the fleet list all have to say "4m ago" the same way — two
/// spellings of the same duration on one screen reads as two different facts.
library;

/// Compact duration formatting shared by the register and the header.
String formatAge(Duration age) {
  if (age.inSeconds < 60) return '${age.inSeconds}s';
  if (age.inMinutes < 60) return '${age.inMinutes}m';
  if (age.inHours < 48) return '${age.inHours}h';

# Feature documentation

One document per feature that exists in the code. [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md)
covers the system: the event-log model, the offline-first ownership split, the
ingest contract, the scale plan, and the ambiguity table. These documents cover
what was actually built and why it looks the way it does.

| # | Feature | Brief | Status |
|---|---------|-------|--------|
| 01 | [Telemetry ingest](01-telemetry-ingest.md) | §2 local-first over DuckDB | Built |
| 02 | [Fleet home](02-fleet-home.md) | §3 A | Built |
| 03 | [Vehicle detail](03-vehicle-detail.md) | §3 B | Built |
| — | Alerts, dismissal, undo | §3 C | Not built |
| — | Geofences | §3 D | Not built |
| — | Automatic trips | §3 E | Not built |
| — | Scale exercise | §4 | Not built |

Every document follows the same shape: what it does, the files, the data flow,
the mechanics, the decisions with their rejected alternatives, the tests that
pin each claim, and what is knowingly left undone.

## Conventions used throughout

**Clean architecture per feature.** `domain` holds entities, repository
interfaces and use cases and imports nothing outward. `data` holds models, data
sources and repository implementations. `presentation` holds a GetX controller,
a binding and widgets. The concrete classes are named in exactly one place per
feature — its `Bindings`.

**GetX for state and injection.** Controllers receive use cases through their
constructors rather than calling `Get.find` internally, so every controller is
directly constructible in a unit test with fakes.

**Event time, never arrival time.** Every rule in the app compares `event_ts`
— when the vehicle measured something — against an injected clock. `ingest_ts`
exists for audit and drives nothing.

**Failures, not exceptions, above the data layer.** Data sources throw
`LocalDatabaseException`; repositories catch it and return `Err(Failure)`.
Nothing in `domain` or `presentation` catches anything.
=== 03 head
# 03 — Vehicle detail

One vehicle: a status header, a readings register with a verdict per signal,
and battery history queried out of the event log.

Covers the brief's §3 B.

## Files

## The readings register

One row per signal, driven by a LEFT JOIN **from `signal_spec`**, so the
register is generated from configuration rather than from a hard-coded list.
Adding a signal to `signal_spec` adds a register row with no code change, and a
signal that has never reported still gets a row — which is exactly the "—, no
pill" case the brief calls for.

```sql
SELECT s.signal, s.label, s.unit, s.max_age_sec, l.value, l.event_ts,
       CASE
         WHEN l.event_ts IS NULL THEN NULL
         WHEN l.event_ts < $1 - to_seconds(s.max_age_sec) THEN 'STALE'
         WHEN (s.crit_lo IS NOT NULL AND l.value < s.crit_lo)
           OR (s.crit_hi IS NOT NULL AND l.value > s.crit_hi)
           OR (s.warn_lo IS NOT NULL AND l.value < s.warn_lo)
           OR (s.warn_hi IS NOT NULL AND l.value > s.warn_hi) THEN 'ALERT'
```

```
           OR (s.warn_hi IS NOT NULL AND l.value > s.warn_hi) THEN 'ALERT'
         ELSE 'NORMAL'
       END AS verdict
FROM signal_spec s
LEFT JOIN vehicle_signal_latest l
  ON l.signal = s.signal AND l.vehicle_id = $2
ORDER BY list_position(
  ['soc', 'range_km', 'speed', 'battery_temp', 'odometer', 'ignition'], s.signal)
```

Order matters and it is deliberate: **staleness is checked before the
thresholds.** A reading of 4 % SOC that arrived forty minutes ago is STALE, not
ALERT. Saying "alert" would assert something about a value we no longer trust,
and saying "normal" would assert the opposite — so STALE refuses to make either
claim. That is why it is a third verdict rather than a flag on the other two,
and why the pill is grey: it is not a milder alert, it is "we do not know".

A signal with no thresholds configured (speed, range, odometer, ignition) can
never be ALERT; it is NORMAL whenever it is fresh.

Display order is a `list_position` expression rather than a `sort_order`
column: ordering is a presentation concern that does not justify a migration.

### The rows

| Row | Notes |
|---|---|
| State of charge, Range, Speed, Battery temperature, Odometer | The five the brief names |
| Ignition | Stored and drives the status ladder, so it is shown. Rendered "On"/"Off" — it rides in a `DOUBLE` column and "1.0" would be technically true and useless |
| Last ping | Rendered in the header, with an age but **no verdict pill** — the status chip beside it already makes the liveness claim, and a second one could contradict it |

Every age on the screen is rendered from the same clock reading the verdicts
were computed against, held on the controller as `evaluatedAt`. A row whose
pill says STALE while its age reads "2s ago" is worse than a clock that only
ticks on refresh.

## Battery history

The one query in the app that touches the multi-million-row event log — which
is the point of the section. The latest-value table cannot answer it.

```sql
SELECT min(event_ts) AS at, avg(value) AS value, count(*) AS n
FROM signal_reading
WHERE vehicle_id = $1 AND signal = 'soc' AND event_ts >= $2
GROUP BY floor((epoch(event_ts) - epoch($3)) / <bucket>)
ORDER BY at
```

Bucketing happens in SQL. Pulling a day of raw readings into Dart to thin them
there would defeat the exercise and would not survive the retained window
growing.

Two details that took a correction each:

* **Bucket width comes from the span the data actually covers**, not from the
  requested window. A vehicle with twenty seconds of history inside a 24-hour
  window otherwise collapses into a single point — which is exactly what the
  first version did on a freshly started app.
* **Buckets are aligned to the first reading**, and the width divides by one
  fewer than the point cap. Aligning to absolute epoch leaves a partial bucket
  at each end, which puts the point count one over the cap. A test caught it.

The chart reports "*N* readings · *M* points · *lo*–*hi* %". Saying how many
raw log rows fed how many plotted points is the honest way to present a
bucketed summary, and it is the visible proof that this came out of the log.

The sparkline is a hand-written `CustomPainter` — one polyline with a fill,
about forty lines. A charting dependency would be more code to audit than the
code it replaces. Its axis is fixed at 0–100 %, not scaled to the data: auto
scaling makes a battery drifting between 61 % and 63 % look like a cliff.

## Controller

One permanent controller whose `open(id)` switches the subject, rather than a
tagged instance per vehicle. Only one detail screen is open at a time, so this
is simpler and leaves nothing to dispose. Opening a different vehicle clears
the previous detail first, so the old vehicle never lingers under the new
header.

An unknown vehicle is `Ok(null)`, not a failure — "no such vehicle" is a normal
answer and gets a not-found message rather than an error screen.

Refresh is the same debounced `DatabasePulse` the fleet list uses.

## 10. Ambiguities and how they are resolved

The brief says the data model has genuinely ambiguous cases. These are the ones I found and the calls I made.

| # | Ambiguity | Resolution | Rejected alternative |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Vehicle is online (odometer 2 min old) but `speed` is 40 min old. MOVING? | Status only reads **fresh** signals; a stale speed cannot claim MOVING or IDLE, so it falls through to STOPPED, the documented fallback bucket. "Fresh" here means the **10-minute OFFLINE window**, not the 5-minute per-signal one — see ambiguity 14. | A sixth `UNKNOWN` chip — the brief specifies five. |
| 2 | What is "last ping"? | `max(event_ts)` across all signals *and* location fixes for the vehicle. | Per-signal freshness only — the brief says vehicle-level. |
| 3 | Event time or arrival time? | **Event time** drives every rule: freshness, status, alerts, transitions, trips. `ingest_ts` is audit only. | Arrival time — makes a backlog dump look like a fleet that just woke up. |
| 4 | What is a duplicate? | Identity is `(vehicle_id, signal, event_ts)`. Same key, different value → keep the first, increment a conflict counter surfaced in a debug view. | Last-write-wins — non-deterministic under reordering, which breaks §0. |
| 5 | Packet older than the retention window | Rejected and counted. It cannot be replayed correctly, so applying it would produce state that no longer follows from the log. | Silently inserting it and leaving derived state inconsistent. |
| 6 | Signal goes stale while an alert is open | Alert stays open, shown with a stale marker. | Auto-resolve — that hides a truck that died at 5 % SOC. |
| 7 | Dismissed at 18 %, then SOC hits 8 % | Escalation clears `dismissed_at` and re-raises. "I am on it" at 18 % is not consent to ignore 8 %. | Staying dismissed through escalation. |
| 8 | UNDO window vs. app kill | Dismissal is persisted immediately; UNDO clears it. Killed mid-window → dismissal stands. | Holding it in memory for 5 s — loses an explicit user action to a crash. |
| 9 | Geofence edited after history exists | Activation is time-versioned; **geometry is not** — a geometry edit recomputes that fence's transitions and affected trips. | Full geometry versioning (correct, more table than this earns) or forward-only edits (cheap, but derived state stops being reproducible from the log). |
| 10 | Vehicle inside two overlapping fences | Containment tracked per fence. UI "current geofence" = smallest radius containing it, tie-break `geofence_id`. | A single current-fence column — undefined under nesting. |
| 11 | Exiting a bay inside a depot | Trips key off containment count reaching 0, so leaving the inner fence starts nothing. | Per-fence exit starts a trip — one departure would produce two trips. |

| 14 | Which freshness window does the status ladder use? | The **vehicle-level 10-minute** window that decides OFFLINE, because status is a vehicle-level claim. The alert badge and the detail-screen verdict pills keep the **per-signal** `signal_spec.max_age_sec`, because a threshold is a claim about one signal. | One window for everything. Scoring the ladder against the 5-minute signal window leaves a dead band between 5 and 10 minutes where an online, visibly moving truck reads STOPPED — caught by a test, not by reasoning. |
| 13 | GPS jitter on the boundary | 25 m (or accuracy, whichever larger) hysteresis band plus two-fix confirmation; band fixes carry the previous zone forward. | Bare `d < r` — flaps a parked truck into dozens of trips. |

## Architecture

Clean architecture per feature (`domain` / `data` / `presentation`) with GetX
for state and dependency injection. `domain` imports nothing outward, so
`IngestController` is unit-tested against a fake repository with no database
involved. See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) §1.

## Status

Built — each with its own document under [docs/](docs/README.md):

* **[Telemetry ingest](docs/01-telemetry-ingest.md)** — packet simulator,
  long-lived writer isolate, staging-table bulk append, duplicate rejection,
  late-packet handling, ingest monitor screen.
* **[Fleet home](docs/02-fleet-home.md)** — vehicle list with registration,
  model, SOC, range, alert badge and status chip; filter chips with live
  counts; empty states. Status and counts are both decided in SQL.
* **[Vehicle detail](docs/03-vehicle-detail.md)** — readings register with a
  NORMAL / ALERT / STALE verdict per signal, and SOC history queried and
  bucketed out of the event log.

Not built: alerts, geofences, trips, the scale exercise (§6–§9 of
ARCHITECTURE.md).

108 tests pass. Three carry the design:

* `test/features/telemetry_ingest/ingest_pipeline_test.dart` — the same feed
  reversed, re-batched and partially redelivered produces byte-identical state
  to the in-order replay.
* `test/features/telemetry_ingest/ingest_binding_test.dart` — building the
  binding actually starts the pipeline and rows reach disk. Every other test
  passed while a running app ingested nothing.
* `test/features/fleet/fleet_end_to_end_test.dart` — simulator to writer
  isolate to DuckDB to the fleet query with nothing stubbed, asserting every
  vehicle lands in exactly one chip.
```

lib/db/alert_sql.dart          the lifecycle — condition, resolve, rescore, raise, dismiss
lib/features/alerts/           13 files, domain · data · presentation

**An alert is an episode, not a flag.** One row is one continuous breach. `severity` moves inside it, `resolved_at` ends it. That shape is what makes the brief's escalation rule fall out for free — 18% → 8% is the same row turning critical, and recovering to 15% walks the same row back down. Two alert types would have needed a suppression rule between them.

**Two rules I got wrong and the running app corrected.** I ran the real macOS build and queried what it left behind: 18 resolutions in 114 seconds, and one truck opening the *same* overheat alert 7 times.

- I had read "thresholds apply to fresh readings only" as a rule about resolving too. It isn't — the brief scopes firing. A truck that went flat at 5% and then stopped reporting is exactly the truck you still want to hear about; auto-resolving deletes the only prompt to act. Resolution now needs evidence: a fresh reading back inside. A quiet signal leaves the episode open and the card says *no fresh reading for 20m · last known 5%*. This was already ambiguity 6 in ARCHITECTURE.md — I'd argued it before writing code, then implemented the opposite.
- The 7-episode truck was sitting on 45.0 °C and wobbling. Resolution now needs the value back inside by a band of 2. Severity inside an open episode keeps the bare thresholds — the episode exists either way, so there are no rows to churn.

Both fixed: re-ran the app, 0 multi-episode pairs out of 6, 0 spurious resolutions. Two overheat alerts are sitting at 44.5 and 44.1 °C — open, inside the band, which is the band visible in the data.

That correction also **deleted code**: nothing in the lifecycle moves without a fresh reading, so the 30-second idle sweep I'd added for the resolve-on-stale rule went with the rule.

**Dismissal** writes to DuckDB before the UNDO appears — not held in memory for five seconds. Local-first means the database is the truth; a crash mid-window should keep the user's action, not evaporate it. Reasons come off the enum so the sheet can't drift from the specified order, "Something else…" opens a note (backing out of *that* cancels the dismissal), and escalation clears a dismissal — "I am on it" at 18% isn't consent to ignore 8%.

**The fleet badge now reads this table** instead of recomputing thresholds in `scoredCte`. `vehicle_status.dart` had a comment promising that swap. Dismissing an alert used to leave its red dot on the list. Cost is honest: the badge is derived state, one pass behind the log.

**Verified:** 167 tests, analyzer clean, real app run twice with the database queried directly both times.

skipped: the readings register still uses bare thresholds, so at 44.5 °C it shows NORMAL beside an open red card — both answers are correct to different questions, but it reads as a bug; documented, and the fix belongs in vehicle detail. Everything uncommitted.

## 7. Geofences and trips

### 6.1 Transition detection

Deterministic pipeline, applied per `(vehicle, geofence)` over event-time-ordered fixes:

1. **Accuracy gate** — discard fixes with `accuracy_m > 100`. Filtered at read; nothing is ever deleted from the log.
2. **Hysteresis** — inside if `d ≤ r − h`, outside if `d ≥ r + h`, with `h = max(25 m, accuracy_m)`. Fixes in the band produce **no zone opinion**.
3. **Carry forward** — `last_value(zone IGNORE NULLS) OVER (PARTITION BY vehicle_id, geofence_id ORDER BY event_ts)`. The band is now genuinely inert rather than a source of flapping.
4. **Confirm** — a crossing is confirmed when two consecutive opinionated fixes agree on the new zone. Escape hatch for a fast exit: one fix more than `2h` past the boundary confirms alone.
5. **Timestamp** — the transition is stamped with the **first** fix of the confirming pair. That is when the vehicle actually crossed.
6. **Gaps** — if the confirming pair straddles a gap > 30 min (the basement case), the transition is still recorded but flagged `confidence = 'low'`, and any trip built on it inherits that flag. Nothing is synthesised across a gap.
7. **Overlaps** — no single "current geofence" internally; containment is per fence. The UI's single-value *current geofence* is the **smallest radius containing the vehicle**, tie-broken by `geofence_id`.
8. **Fence activation** is time-versioned via `active_from` / `active_to`, so evaluation asks "was this fence active at the fix's event time" and recompute stays pure. **Geometry is not versioned** — editing centre or radius triggers a full recompute of that fence's transitions and the affected trips. Full geometry versioning is the upgrade if fences turn out to be edited often; it is not worth the table for this exercise.

All of steps 2–6 are expressible with `lag`/`last_value IGNORE NULLS` window functions — set-based, no row-at-a-time Dart fold.

### 6.2 Trips

A nested fence must not manufacture a trip: leaving a bay while still inside the depot is not a departure. So trips key off **containment count**, not individual fences:

```sql
SELECT *, sum(CASE kind WHEN 'ENTRY' THEN 1 ELSE -1 END)
            OVER (PARTITION BY vehicle_id ORDER BY event_ts) AS inside_count
FROM geofence_transition
```

- `inside_count` falling to **0** → trip starts; origin = the fence just exited.
- `inside_count` rising off 0 → active trip completes; destination = the fence just entered. Returning to origin is a normal completion.
- Still 0 at the end of the stream → `IN_PROGRESS`. No timeout; a truck that never reports again keeps an open trip, which is the truthful representation.
- One active trip per vehicle falls out of the model for free.
- Incremental recompute seeds `inside_count` from the containment state at the window start.

`distance_km` comes from an `ASOF JOIN` onto the odometer log at `start_ts` and `end_ts`; NULL when the odometer is missing rather than guessed.

**Idempotency.** `trip_id = hash(vehicle_id, start_ts)`, so a duplicate packet regenerates the identical row. A late packet that moves a boundary is handled by the replay in §4 step 4 — delete derived rows at or after `t0`, re-derive — with the deterministic id as the backstop, not the mechanism.

  TelemetryPacket _emit(_SimulatedVehicle vehicle, DateTime now) {

      );
    }
    if (_tickCount % 4 == 0) {
      signals['odometer'] = double.parse(vehicle.odometer.toStringAsFixed(2));

    // usually good and occasionally terrible — the bad fixes are what the

          )
        : null;

      eventTs: now,
      signals: signals,

/// Knobs for the packet simulator.
///
/// The fault rates are the point of the whole thing: a feed that behaves
/// perfectly proves nothing about a pipeline built to survive one that does
/// not. Defaults are deliberately nastier than a real fleet so the
/// duplicate/late counters move visibly within seconds.
class SimulatorConfig {
  const SimulatorConfig({
    this.vehicleCount = 40,
    this.tick = const Duration(milliseconds: 500),
    this.duplicateRate = 0.08,
    this.lateRate = 0.10,
    this.dropRate = 0.03,
    this.backlogChance = 0.004,
    this.backlogTicks = 20,
    this.seed = 1337,
  });

  /// Fleet size. 500 for the scale exercise; a few dozen for a readable demo.
  final int vehicleCount;

  /// How often the simulated fleet emits.
  final Duration tick;

  /// Fraction of packets delivered twice — the network retrying, not the
  /// vehicle measuring twice. The duplicate carries an identical event time,
  /// which is what makes the natural key able to reject it.
  final double duplicateRate;

  /// Fraction of packets held back and released a few ticks later, still
  /// stamped with their original event time. This is out-of-order arrival.
  final double lateRate;

  /// Fraction of packets that never arrive at all.
  final double dropRate;

  /// Per-vehicle per-tick chance of going dark (a basement) and buffering.
  final double backlogChance;

  /// How many ticks a dark vehicle stays dark before dumping its backlog.
  final int backlogTicks;

  /// Fixes every random decision, so a test run is reproducible and a failure
  /// can be replayed exactly.
  final int seed;
}

This is what lets an\n///   incremental pass read two fixes instead of a whole history.\n/// * `seq`     \u2014 `lag` over the opinionated sequence only.\n/// * `decided` \u2014 a crossing is confirmed by **two consecutive opinionated\n///   fixes agreeing**, or by a single fix more than `2h` clear of the boundary\n///   (step 4: a truck doing 60 through a fence edge should not need a second\n///   fix to prove it left).\n/// * `settled` \u2014 carry the confirmed zone forward with `last_value ... IGNORE\n///   NULLS`, so each row knows the zone that was established *before* it.\n///\n/// A transition is emitted where a confirmation disagrees with the established\n/// zone. It is stamped with the **first** fix of the confirming pair, which is\n/// when the vehicle actually crossed, not when we became sure (step 5).\n///\n/// The first confirmation on a cold start establishes a zone and emits\n/// nothing: we have learned where the truck is, not watched it go there.\nconst geofenceTransitionQuery =\n    '''\nWITH probe AS (\n  SELECT l.vehicle_id,\n         g.geofence_id,\n         l.event_ts,\n         $_distanceMetres AS d,\n         g.radius_m,\n         greatest($minimumBandMetres, coalesce(l.accuracy_m, 0)) AS band\n  FROM location_fix l\n  JOIN staging_geo_scope s\n    ON s.vehicle_id = l.vehicle_id AND l.event_ts >= s.from_ts\n  JOIN geofence g\n    ON l.event_ts >= g.active_from\n   AND (g.active_to IS NULL OR l.event_ts < g.active_to)\n  WHERE coalesce(l.accuracy_m, 0) <= $accuracyGateMetres\n),\nopinion AS (\n  SELECT vehicle_id,\n         geofence_id,\n         event_ts,\n         CASE WHEN d <= radius_m - band THEN 'IN'\n              WHEN d >= radius_m + band THEN 'OUT' END AS zone,\n         abs(d - radius_m) > 2 * band AS decisive,\n         FALSE AS is_seed,\n         CAST(NULL AS TEXT) AS seed_zone\n  FROM probe\n),\nseeded AS (\n  SELECT c.vehicle_id,\n         c.geofence_id,\n         c.pending_ts AS event_ts,\n         c.pending_zone AS zone,\n         FALSE AS decisive,\n         TRUE AS is_seed,\n         c.zone AS seed_zone\n  FROM geofence_containment c\n  JOIN staging_geo_scope s ON s.vehicle_id = c.vehicle_id\n  WHERE c.pending_zone IS NOT NULL AND c.pending_ts < s.from_ts\n),\nordered AS (\n  SELECT * FROM opinion WHERE zone IS NOT NULL\n  UNION ALL\n  SELECT * FROM seeded\n),\nseq AS (\n  SELECT *,\n         lag(zone)     OVER w AS prev_zone,\n         lag(event_ts) OVER w AS prev_ts\n  FROM ordered\n  WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY vehicle_id, geofence_id ORDER BY event_ts)\n),\ndecided AS (\n  SELECT *,\n         CASE\n           WHEN is_seed THEN seed_zone\n           WHEN zone = prev_zone OR decisive THEN zone\n         END AS confirmed_zone,\n         CASE WHEN zone = prev_zone THEN prev_ts ELSE event_ts END AS crossed_ts\n  FROM seq\n),\nsettled AS (\n  SELECT *,\n         last_value(confirmed_zone IGNORE NULLS) OVER (\n           PARTITION BY vehicle_id, geofence_id ORDER BY event_ts\n           ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING\n         ) AS prior_zone\n  FROM decided\n)\n''';\n\n/// Writes the confirmed crossings.\n///\n/// `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` against `(vehicle_id, geofence_id, event_ts)`\n/// rather than as the deduplication mechanism: the delete above already\n/// cleared the range being rewritten. What this catches is the one transition\n/// that can land *before* the window \u2014 a pair whose first fix was already\n/// folded in as the seed \u2014 which is a genuine crossing we simply could not\n/// confirm last time.\nconst insertGeofenceTransitions =\n    '''\n$geofenceTransitionQuery\nINSERT INTO geofence_transition\nSELECT vehicle_id,\n       geofence_id,\n       crossed_ts,\n       CASE confirmed_zone WHEN 'IN' THEN 'ENTRY' ELSE 'EXIT' END,\n       CASE WHEN prev_ts IS NULL\n                 OR event_ts - prev_ts > $gapConfidenceCutoff\n            THEN 'low' ELSE 'high' END\nFROM settled\nWHERE NOT is_seed\n  AND confirmed_zone IS NOT NULL\n  AND prior_zone IS NOT NULL\n  AND confirmed_zone <> prior_zone\nON CONFLICT DO NOTHING\n''';\n\n/// Folds the pass's end state back into the containment table.\n///\n/// One row per (vehicle, fence): the zone established by the end of the\n/// window, and the last fix that had an opinion at all. The next pass resumes\n/// from exactly here, which is the entire reason an ingest batch costs two\n/// fixes of work rather than a history.\nconst upsertGeofenceContainment =\n    '''\n$geofenceTransitionQuery\nINSERT INTO geofence_containment AS c\nSELECT vehicle_id,\n       geofence_id,\n       coalesce(confirmed_zone, prior_zone),\n       zone,\n       event_ts\nFROM settled\nQUALIFY row_number() OVER (\n  PARTITION BY vehicle_id, geofence_id ORDER BY event_ts DESC\n) = 1\nON CONFLICT (vehicle_id, geofence_id) DO UPDATE\n  SET zone = excluded.zone,\n      pending_zone = excluded.pending_zone,\n      pending_ts = excluded.pending_ts\n''';\n\n/// Runs one derivation pass over whatever is in `staging_geo_scope`.\n///\n/// Public, and here rather than in the writer, so the tests drive the same\n/// four statements in the same order production does.\nFuture<void> deriveGeofences(Connection conn) async {\n  await conn.execute(deleteScopedTransitions);\n  await conn.execute(deleteReplayedContainment);\n  await conn.execute(insertGeofenceTransitions);\n  await conn.execute(upsertGeofenceContainment);\n}\n\n/// Scopes every vehicle for a full replay and re-derives.\n///\n/// What a fence edit triggers. It recomputes *all* fences, not just the one\n/// that changed, and that is deliberate: derived state is dropped and rebuilt\n/// (\u00a73.5), and one path that is always right beats two that are usually\n/// right. Editing a fence is rare, user-initiated, and can afford to be slow;\n/// a subtly wrong incremental path cannot.\nFuture<void> recomputeAllGeofences(Connection conn) async {\n  await conn.execute(geofenceScopeDdl);\n  await conn.execute(clearGeofenceScope);\n  await conn.execute(insertGeofenceScopeAll);\n  await deriveGeofences(conn);\n}\nDART\ndart format lib/db/geofence_sql.dart >/dev/null && flutter analyze lib/db 2>&1 | tail -3",
  "description": "Write the geofence detector SQL"
}
